 Plan: Add greet(name) to greet.py                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                        
 Context                                                                          
                                                                                                                                        
 The project has one existing file (existing.py) with a single print statement. The user wants a new greet.py with a greet(name) function
 that prints a greeting message.

 Implementation

 Create /tmp/plantest2/greet.py with:

 def greet(name):
     print(f"Hello, {name}!")

 - Uses an f-string for the greeting (modern Python style)
 - Double quotes match the existing code convention in existing.py
 - No imports needed

 Verification

 Run in the terminal:
 python3 -c "from greet import greet; greet('World')"
 Expected output: Hello, World!
